You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Applied Materials (AMAT) Fiscal Q3 2026 Earnings Highlights: Record Revenue and Profits, 13th Consecutive Quarter of Gross Margin Expansion, Strong Q4 Guidance Beats Expectations — Yet Stock Falls on “Sell the News” Reaction

TEXT:
Core Viewpoint
Applied Materials delivered a comprehensively better-than-expected Q3 report: revenue of $9.12 billion hit a company record (up 25% year-over-year), adjusted EPS of $3.50 also set a record (up 41% YoY), and GAAP gross margin reached 50.3% (up 1.5 percentage points YoY, the 13th consecutive quarter of year-over-year improvement). Semiconductor Systems was the primary growth engine, with AI-driven long-term demand visibility extending to 2030. The company raised its calendar 2026 packaging revenue growth outlook to more than 70%. Despite the strong beat on both results and Q4 guidance, the stock fell approximately 3–5% after hours, reflecting that after a more-than-doubling rally over the past year, the market’s appetite for “beats” has been stretched to the limit — turning “good numbers, bad stock reaction” into the new normal for AI equipment names.
Specific Breakdown
1. Overall Revenue and Profit Performance
Revenue of $9.12 billion exceeded analyst expectations of roughly $9.0 billion (FactSet consensus around $8.99–9.0 billion), setting a company record and rising 25% year-over-year.
Adjusted EPS of $3.50 also set a record, up 41% year-over-year; GAAP EPS was $3.17, up 43%.
GAAP gross margin of 50.3%, up 1.5 percentage points year-over-year; non-GAAP gross margin of 50.4%.
Record operating income (GAAP approximately $3.08 billion at 33.7% margin; non-GAAP approximately $3.10 billion at 34.0% margin), with continued margin expansion.
Record cash from operations of about $3.04 billion; returned approximately $860 million to shareholders ($440 million in share repurchases + $420 million in dividends).
2. Semiconductor Systems Performance
Revenue of $7.04 billion, up approximately 30% year-over-year (from about $5.56 billion in the prior-year period), serving as the quarter’s core growth engine.
Mix: Foundry/Logic and other ~67%, DRAM ~26%, Flash ~7%.
Gross margin of 55.3%, up 1.9 percentage points year-over-year; operating margin improved from 33.0% to 37.7%.
Key drivers: “Unprecedented” demand for materials engineering solutions fueled by rapid global AI adoption; customers urging faster equipment delivery and capacity increases; strong demand in leading-edge logic, foundry, and DRAM.
3. Other Business Segment Performance
Applied Global Services revenue of $1.78 billion, up 11% year-over-year.
Growth supported by higher fab utilization rates and an expanding installed base, with customers selecting more advanced services to boost output and yield.
4. Future Plans and Growth Outlook
The company now expects its semiconductor equipment business to grow more than 30% in calendar 2026, and packaging revenue growth of more than 70% (raised from the prior outlook of more than 50%).
CEO Gary Dickerson stated that customer demand visibility continues to increase and that Applied Materials expects another strong growth year in 2027. Customers are requesting higher capacity and accelerated tool deliveries; some conversations already extend to 2030. Major customers are providing rolling eight-quarter demand forecasts.
CFO Brice Hill noted that second-half revenue growth is expected to remain strong, particularly in DRAM, advanced logic/foundry, and advanced packaging.
5. Next-Quarter Guidance (Fiscal Q4 2026)
Revenue midpoint of approximately $10.25 billion (range $9.75–10.75 billion), roughly 7% above analyst consensus (around $9.55–9.66 billion) and implying about 51% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
Adjusted EPS midpoint of $4.02 (range $3.82–4.22), also above market expectations.
Non-GAAP gross margin expected at about 50.4%, flat with Q3.
Semiconductor Systems expected at roughly $7.9 billion; Applied Global Services at about $1.84 billion.
6. Market Backdrop and Investor Concerns
Core tension: Consecutive beats have become the base case rather than a positive surprise. Applied Materials shares are up about 108% year-to-date and roughly 194% over the past year — approaching the best annual performance since 1999. After such gains, the market now requires “substantial” beats to drive the stock higher.
Sector rotation and profit-taking: The semiconductor equipment group has recently pulled back amid questions about the sustainability of AI capital spending. Applied Materials has been consolidating for about six weeks since its June 30 all-time high. Peer KLA’s earlier “in-line” results also led to a stock decline, raising the bar for the entire group.
Investor reaction: The roughly 3–5% after-hours decline reflects that while fundamentals remain solid and growth momentum is intact, the results were not enough to immediately impress Wall Street. Analysts note that if the strong trajectory continues, 2027 consensus estimates still have room to move higher. This is not a deterioration in fundamentals, but rather an inflation of expectations — market patience is being tested by ever-rising bars.
